name: Shingle Row week
summary: A silent week on the marsh for thirty experienced practitioners with a teacher who gives a morning talk, meets each person every other day, and leads two sits. Days otherwise unplanned. £540.
description:
Shingle Row is a former coastguard row on the edge of the marsh, six cottages and a long room, and every September and May thirty people spend a silent week there.

The week is led by Anja, who has taught in the insight tradition for twenty years but does not teach in a tradition here. She gives a talk in the long room each morning at nine, about forty minutes, and leads a sit at seven and at six. Every second day she meets each person alone for twenty minutes, and those conversations are where the week does its work for most people. She is around between, on the sea wall or in the long room, and can be approached.

Nothing is required. The talk and the two sits are offered, and most people come to most of them, but if you are on the marsh at nine, nobody will fetch you. The days between have no shape: the marsh, the shingle, the cottages, the long room.

Silence is kept for the whole week, apart from the meetings with Anja. Meals are in the long room, in silence, at fixed times.

It is a restful week. The marsh is flat, the sits are not long, and the sea air does most of the work. We ask that people have a settled practice and have done at least one residential retreat of five days; the week assumes you can hold silence and unstructured time without help, and Anja's talks assume a working vocabulary.
practical: Saturday to Saturday, one week in May and one in September. £540 including all meals and a shared room; single rooms £680. Six cottages, two or three to a cottage. Bring boots, waterproofs, binoculars if you have them, and warm layers; the wind is constant. Sheringham station is nine miles; we collect. No signal in the cottages; some on the sea wall.
